newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania cabinet approves state bank selloff bill.
newsitem.headline: Romania cabinet approves state bank selloff bill.

text.p: Romania's centrist coalition government on Monday approved a bank privatisation bill, as part of broader reform agreed with international lenders for renewed funding support.
"The bill will be sent to parliament and I hope it will pass by the end of this month," Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu said.
The ruling coalition, which ousted leftists in last year's elections, has a comfortable majority in parliament.
The bank selloff bill, a key part of previous loan accords with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, failed to clear parliament twice in 1996.
Spineanu said Banca Romana pentru Dezvoltare SA development bank would be the first of six state-run banks to go private after the bill came into force.

The long-awaited privatisation will proceed by a combination of raising bank capital through private or public share issues and sales of stocks held by the majority shareholder, the State Ownership Fund.

Any share acquisition larger than five percent must be approved by the central bank. "The state is allowed to retain 10 percent of the banks' stock, to be called a golden share giving it veto rights in certain decisions," Spineanu said.

The banking sector, made up of 40 commercial banks, is one of the fastest growing in post-communist Romania. But the country's fledgling financial markets have been buffeted in recent years by scandals at two private banks, which now await court ruling on their fate -- liquidation or reorganisation.
